blogs.title: The Lung Mask: How a Pancreatic Injury Manifests as Bloody Pleural Effusion in Children
blogs.description: Explore the case of a 12‑year‑old boy who presented solely with right‑sided chest pain and recurrent haemorrhagic effusions, only to turn out a pancreatopleural fistula after a bicycle‑handle trauma. Highlight the diagnostic blind spots in pediatric pleural disease, the importance of a meticulous history, and how abdominal pathology can masquerade as a respiratory emergency.

blogs.title: Pleural Fluid Amylase: The ‘Pancreatic Whisperer’ You Should Never Ignore
blogs.description: Delve into the key biochemical clue that tipped the scales in this case—the pleural fluid amylase level of 6,118 IU/L. Discuss the threshold, differentiate pancreatic from salivary amylase, contrast it with tuberculosis, malignancy, or esophageal rupture, and outline a practical algorithm for interpreting pleural fluid in adults and children.

blogs.title: Imaging the Passage: Navigating Chest CT, MRCP, and ERCP to Visualize Pancreatopleural Fistulas
blogs.description: Compare the strengths and pitfalls of each imaging modality in diagnosing PPF. Emphasize how CT hinted at a retroperitoneal collection, MRCP confirmed the ductal communication, and why ERCP remains the gold standard for therapeutic planning—illustrated through the imaging progression in this rare pediatric case.

blogs.title: Conservative Curatives: Why Octreotide and Total Parenteral Nutrition Win in Pediatric PPF
blogs.description: Review the evidence behind non‑surgical treatment—nil per‑oral, TPN, octreotide infusion, and pancreatic enzyme replacement. Examine dosing strategies, success rates, and the mechanisms that promote fistula closure, with a focus on the 10‑day healing course that resolved the child’s effusions.

blogs.title: Genetic Underpinnings: Why Pediatric Pancreatitis and PPF Should Prompt a Molecular Workup
blogs.description: Highlight the role of hereditary mutations (PRSS1, SPINK1, CFTR, CFTR) in pediatric pancreatitis, linking them to the development of complications such as PPF. Discuss family screening, surveillance strategies, and how early genetic insight can alter prognosis and guide lifelong management.
